rv.q: It is three days before anyone even notices. That sounds like a spoiler, but it happens surprisingly early in a play that is less about a worthless death than a meaningful life. Surviving him is his cellmate and childhood friend Sean Molloy, good-natured despite circumstance dealing him a bad hand.
Directed by Jake Sleet, it rarely misses a beat, the laughs come easily and the suspense builds as the plot and the lads' relationship begins to twist.
It is Sean Connor as an irrepressible Davie, however, who drives things with a charisma that makes you understand why Sean falls under his spell.
